officialTitle: Capivasertib in Hormone Receptor-Positive Advanced Breast Cancer
setting: Advanced disease relapsed or progressed during or after aromatase inhibitor, with or without prior CDK4/6 inhibitor

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: Overall, 708 patients underwent randomization; 289 patients (40.8%) had AKT pathway alterations, and 489 (69.1%) had received a CDK4/6 inhibitor previously for advanced breast cancer.
design.notes: 1:1 randomisation. Enrolled pre-, peri- and postmenopausal women and men. AKT pathway alteration denotes PIK3CA, AKT1 or PTEN alterations (gene symbols stripped in PubMed abstract text).

sponsor: AstraZeneca and the National Cancer Institute
clinicalQuestion: Does adding the AKT inhibitor capivasertib to fulvestrant improve PFS in HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer after aromatase inhibitor therapy, overall and in AKT pathway-altered tumours?

pico.population: HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer with relapse or progression during/after an aromatase inhibitor, with or without prior CDK4/6 inhibitor
pico.outcomes: Dual primary: investigator-assessed PFS in overall and AKT pathway-altered populations. Safety

publications.title: Capivasertib in Hormone Receptor-Positive Advanced Breast Cancer.
publications.label: Primary analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: In the overall population, the median progression-free survival was 7.2 months in the capivasertib-fulvestrant group, as compared with 3.6 months in the placebo-fulvestrant group (hazard ratio for progression or death, 0.60; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.51 to 0.71; P<0.001).

In the AKT pathway-altered population, the median progression-free survival was 7.3 months in the capivasertib-fulvestrant group, as compared with 3.1 months in the placebo-fulvestrant group (hazard ratio, 0.50; 95% CI, 0.38 to 0.65; P<0.001).

safety.sourceQuote: The most frequent adverse events of grade 3 or higher in patients receiving capivasertib-fulvestrant were rash (in 12.1% of patients, vs. in 0.3% of those receiving placebo-fulvestrant) and diarrhea (in 9.3% vs. 0.3%).

The most frequent adverse events of grade 3 or higher in patients receiving capivasertib-fulvestrant were rash (in 12.1% of patients, vs. in 0.3% of those receiving placebo-fulvestrant) and diarrhea (in 9.3% vs. 0.3%).
Adverse events leading to discontinuation were reported in 13.0% of the patients receiving capivasertib and in 2.3% of those receiving placebo.

strengths: Majority of patients had prior CDK4/6 inhibitor, reflecting contemporary practice
Dual primary endpoints in overall and biomarker-defined populations
limitations: Benefit in non-altered tumours not separately reported in the abstract
OS not reported in the primary publication

clinicalImplications.text: Supports capivasertib plus fulvestrant after aromatase inhibitor therapy (with or without prior CDK4/6 inhibitor) in HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer, with PFS benefit in both the overall and AKT pathway-altered populations.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Test for PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN alterations at progression on endocrine therapy; rash and diarrhoea are the main grade 3 toxicities to anticipate with capivasertib.

curation.notes: Numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 37256976. The PubMed abstract text strips italic gene symbols in '(,, or)'; PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN attribution should be confirmed against the full text.
